items.headline: Friday sell-off: Nasdaq falls 2.86%, S&P 500 1.82%, Dow about 1.1%
items.note: Both the Nasdaq and S&P 500 had their worst day since June, and the Nasdaq ended October with its worst monthly fall since March 2025. A chip index dropped 7.2% as worries about AI spending grew. Markets are closed for the weekend, so this is still the latest close.

items.headline: Intel falls 28.58%, its worst day since 1974, after a weak forecast
items.note: Intel guided Q4 revenue to $15-16B and adjusted EPS to $0.25 versus $0.43 expected by analysts. Data center and AI revenue rose 78%, but PC sales fell 5% and the company expects that slowdown to last into next year.

items.headline: Amazon's AI spending pushes trailing free cash flow to a $42.4B outflow
items.note: Q3 EPS of $1.89 missed the $1.96 estimate, though AWS grew 39% and sales rose 12% to $201.9B. The stock slid as much as about 7% before the open but closed down 1.41%. Investors now watch whether AI spending turns into profit.

items.headline: Anthropic files a public S-1 for an IPO, planning a Nasdaq listing as 'ANT'
items.note: The filing was reported as submitted Oct 26. Share count and price range are not set and it is not yet effective, so timing is open. A wave of AI IPOs could change how AI companies pay and hire. I read this in secondary reports, not the SEC filing.

items.headline: Fed has already hiked this year; markets are watching for more
items.note: An early-October analysis said Chair Kevin Warsh cited inflation for a September 16 hike, and futures priced a possible second hike. The next jobs report is Dec 4, five days before the Dec 9 Fed decision. This is market pricing, not a Fed decision.

items.headline: Okta joins the S&P 500 on November 4, replacing Kenvue
items.note: Index membership is decided by committee and changes a few times a year. Funds that track the index must buy the new stock and sell the removed one.

learn.explain: Guidance is a company's own forecast of its upcoming revenue, profit or margins. Stocks trade on expectations about the future, so guidance often moves a share price more than last quarter's results. Intel's Q3 revenue was $16.5B, but it guided Q4 to $15-16B and EPS of $0.25 versus the $0.43 analysts expected, and the stock fell 28.58%. A gap between guidance and analyst expectations is often what drives a big one-day move.
